title: Amazon and Walmart Thought India Would Be Their Next Giant Market. India’s Shopkeepers Would Like to Disagree
summary: Indian shopkeepers are protesting against Amazon and Walmart's e-commerce operations, alleging predatory pricing and violation of regulations designed to protect local businesses. This conflict arises as India investigates these allegations, and local merchants, a significant political force, lobby the government to protect their interests from the global giants. The shopkeepers claim that e-commerce deep discounting is driving them out of business, despite earlier regulatory changes aimed at leveling the playing field.

title: Rigetti Quantum Computers Now Available via Amazon Web Services
summary: Rigetti Computing announced its quantum computers are now available through Amazon Braket, a new fully managed Amazon Web Services (AWS) solution. This collaboration significantly expands access to Rigetti's quantum systems, allowing scientists, researchers, and developers to experiment with their 32-qubit superconducting chip technology. Rigetti has also joined the AWS Partner Network to develop quantum computing applications for enterprise customers.

title: Weak Brick-and-Mortar Holiday Shopping Can Fuel "CLIX" ETF
summary: Online shopping surged for Black Friday, leading to a 6% drop in sales for brick-and-mortar stores. This trend suggests potential gains for the Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX), which invests in online retailers and shorts physical stores. The article also mentions the Direxion Daily Retail Bull 3X ETF (RETL) for those bullish on retail sales during the Christmas season.

title: Amazon’s AWS Will Now Power FOX’s Streaming Services Including FOX Sports
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has partnered with FOX to power all of FOX’s streaming services, including the FOX Sports app, and the backend for over 200 affiliate FOX stations. This collaboration aims to enhance the delivery of live sports, news, and entertainment through AWS Media Services, AWS Outposts for on-premises video processing, and AWS analytics and machine learning services for improved user experiences. FOX anticipates increased quality and reliability for its streaming services and affiliates as a result of this extended partnership.

title: Microsoft Security—a Leader in 5 Gartner Magic Quadrants
summary: Microsoft Security has been recognized as a Leader in five Gartner Magic Quadrants across various security areas including Cloud Access Security Brokers (CASB), Access Management, Enterprise Information Archiving, Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) tools, and Endpoint Protection Platforms. This recognition highlights the breadth and depth of Microsoft's security offerings, emphasizing their integrated approach that works across different cloud environments and non-Microsoft solutions. The article details Microsoft's strengths in each of these five categories, showcasing their commitment to providing comprehensive and integrated security solutions.

title: Intel in talks to buy Israeli AI chip co Habana Labs
summary: Intel is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire Israeli AI chip startup Habana Labs for an estimated $1 billion. Habana Labs, founded in 2016, previously raised $120 million, with Intel Capital leading its latest financing round in November 2018. If the acquisition proceeds, it would significantly strengthen Intel's position in the AI chip market, where Habana Labs has developed specialized AI Training and Inference Processors.

title: It’s hard for shoppers to avoid Amazon — even in their investments
summary: This article discusses the challenge for investors to avoid Amazon's influence, even in diversified portfolios, due to its pervasive market presence. It emphasizes the importance of understanding what one is investing in, particularly when considering the consumer discretionary sector. The piece also raises the question of whether consumer discretionary or consumer staples companies are better investments depending on the economic outlook.

title: iHeartmedia Picks Nashville For Second Headquarters for iHeartRadio Digital
summary: iHeartMedia has announced Nashville, Tennessee, will be the location for its second digital headquarters for iHeartRadio, set to open in 2020. Company officials cited Nashville's thriving technology ecosystem, rich music history, and entrepreneurial spirit as key factors in their decision to expand beyond their New York headquarters. This move is expected to create new jobs in engineering, product development, and data science, further strengthening iHeartRadio's position as a leading audio company.

title: Fox to Use Amazon Web Services for Cable, Satellite Broadcasts
summary: Fox Corp. is partnering with Amazon Web Services for its cable and satellite broadcasts, turning to Amazon's cloud to route video to its customers. This multi-year deal involves AWS Media Services transmitting Fox sports, news, and entertainment content, and also helping power Fox production facilities. The move aims to replace Fox's older video infrastructure with a more agile system capable of adapting to business changes and launching new channels quicker.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO reveals 2020 tech plans at Amazon event, guest DJs
summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon addressed attendees at Amazon.com Inc.’s cloud-tech conference in Las Vegas to discuss the bank's 2020 tech plans. He was also guest DJ at the event.

title: How Amazon created AWS and changed technology forever
summary: This article details how Amazon Web Services (AWS) originated from Amazon's internal need to scale its e-commerce operations beyond books. AWS established the cloud computing industry, transforming technology and becoming a multi-billion-dollar market leader. However, it now faces significant competition from Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud.

title: Ross Dress for Less set to grow here
summary: Ross Dress for Less is expanding into Northeast Ohio as part of its Ohio expansion program, with its first store already open in Cuyahoga Falls and additional stores planned for Brooklyn and Mentor. The off-price apparel and home goods chain is seen as a welcome addition to the region's retail real estate market, with estimates suggesting at least nine more stores could open in the Cleveland and Akron areas. This expansion leverages the void left by other retailers and aims to provide an accessible shopping option for consumers.

title: Chesapeake Utilities to buy Elkton Gas for $15M
summary: Chesapeake Utilities Corp. has agreed to acquire Elkton Gas for $15 million from South Jersey Industries (SJI). This acquisition is expected to close in the second quarter of 2020 and will expand Chesapeake Utilities' natural gas service area in Cecil County, Maryland. SJI's sale of Elkton Gas is part of its strategy to refocus on its core business in New Jersey.

title: VanEck Retail ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:RTH) $RTH
summary: The VanEck Retail ETF (RTH) tracks the MVIS US Listed Retail 25 index, consisting of the 25 largest US-listed retail companies. As of March 20, 2026, its price was $245.65, representing a 1.6% decrease since the beginning of the year. The ETF has $243.57 million in assets under management and its top holdings include Amazon, Walmart, and Costco.

title: Kids' Smartwatches Sold on Amazon Can Be Easily Hacked by Strangers
summary: Cybersecurity researchers Rapid7 have found critical security flaws in cheap kids' smartwatches sold on Amazon, allowing strangers to easily track and communicate with children. These devices, which are often white-label rebrands, have ineffective security measures such as faulty whitelists and easily discoverable default passwords. Parents are advised to stick with recognizable brands to avoid these security risks.

title: Teamsters Strike UNFI, Supplier to Whole Foods
summary: Teamsters Local 414 members initiated a strike at a UNFI distribution center in Fort Wayne, Indiana, protesting alleged violations of workers' rights and failure to bargain in good faith. The strike by 158 workers, who supply groceries in six states, highlights UNFI's troubled labor history and its stock decline since acquiring SUPERVALU. As UNFI's largest customer, with 21% of its 2019 revenue, Whole Foods/Amazon will be impacted by the strike.

title: Amazon Logistics parcel volume will surpass UPS and FedEx by 2022, Morgan Stanley says
summary: Morgan Stanley predicts that Amazon Logistics' parcel volume will exceed that of UPS and FedEx by 2022, primarily handling its own orders but also with an expected expansion into third-party logistics. Amazon's current growth rate of delivering its own orders suggests it will overtake legacy carriers despite focusing mainly on densely populated areas. The report also highlights the importance of Amazon's logistics expansion for its profitability and its potential to significantly reduce the market share of traditional parcel carriers.

title: Amazon Is Leaving Rural Deliveries to USPS: Morgan Stanley
summary: A Morgan Stanley report reveals that Amazon Logistics is focusing on lucrative urban and suburban delivery areas, leaving less profitable rural deliveries to the USPS. This strategy helps Amazon slash costs for its expanding transportation network but further strains the financially struggling USPS, which is legally obligated to serve all US addresses. Amazon's "cherry-picking" of dense zip codes means it's avoiding the high costs associated with rural deliveries, putting the USPS in a more difficult financial position.

title: Intel Buys Israeli AI Chipmaker Habana Labs for $2 Billion
summary: Intel Corp. acquired Israeli AI chipmaker Habana Labs for approximately $2 billion to strengthen its position in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence silicon market. This acquisition is part of Intel's strategy to make its offerings essential to major silicon buyers and compete against companies like Alphabet's Google and Amazon's AWS, which are increasingly designing their own chips for data centers. Habana Labs is expected to operate independently for the time being.

title: The Curious Case of Kroger and Walgreens
summary: Kroger and Walgreens have formed an unprecedented Retail Procurement Alliance, leading to speculation about a potential merger between the two companies. Such a merger would create a retail giant with $257 billion in annual revenues and over 12,000 stores, offering significant synergies and enhanced competitiveness against market leaders like Walmart and Amazon. The article draws parallels to Kroger's 1998 merger with Fred Meyer, highlighting a history of strategic deal-making to address competitive threats.

title: Dave Clark: The Man Who Built Amazon’s Delivery Machine
summary: This article profiles Dave Clark, the executive responsible for building Amazon's massive delivery network. It details his aggressive tactics and strategic decisions, including reducing reliance on partners like FedEx and UPS, investing heavily in warehouses and logistics, and grappling with challenges like worker safety and rapid growth. The piece highlights how Clark's vision has shaped Amazon's delivery capabilities, even as the company faces increasing scrutiny and operational hurdles.

title: Amazon hits back at claims it’s abusing open-source software
summary: Amazon Web Services Inc. has responded to criticism that it "strip-mines" open-source software projects by repackaging them as paid services. While AWS claims to be giving customers what they want and contributing significantly to open-source projects, some critics argue this practice undermines the sustainability of open-source companies, forcing them to compete against the very software they developed. Analysts suggest open-source companies must innovate and offer managed versions of their products to succeed against large cloud providers.

title: F5 Networks will acquire Shape Security for $1 billion to bolster online fraud protection services
summary: F5 Networks announced its acquisition of Shape Security for approximately $1 billion to enhance its online fraud protection services and strengthen its application security portfolio. This is F5's largest acquisition to date, following its earlier purchase of NGINX, and is expected to significantly boost F5's software revenue growth. Shape Security brings advanced machine learning and AI capabilities, mitigating over 1 billion fake transactions daily for a clientele including Fortune 50 companies, major banks, and airlines.

title: ETF of the Week: ProShares's ONLN ETF
summary: This article features CEO Tom Lydon discussing the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN) on his "ETF of the Week" podcast. ONLN tracks a modified market-capitalization weighted index of global online retailers, including major players like Amazon and Alibaba, and aims to capitalize on the increasing trend of online shopping. Lydon highlights the potential for growth in online retail, despite concerns about market fluctuations, suggesting ONLN could be a viable investment for both long-term and shorter-term strategies.

title: Amazon to deliver 3.5 billion packages through own network in 2019
summary: Amazon announced it was on track to deliver 3.5 billion customer packages globally in 2019 through its in-house delivery network, indicating its growing independence from third-party shippers like FedEx and UPS. A Morgan Stanley analysis estimated Amazon's logistics would handle 6.5 billion packages by 2022, surpassing both UPS and FedEx. The company also confirmed it now has 150 U.S. delivery stations employing over 90,000 people.

title: Urban Edge acquires Wonderland Marketplace for $24.1 million - Heald and Angelone of JLL represent the seller
summary: Urban Edge Properties has acquired Wonderland Marketplace, a 139,507 s/f shopping center in Revere, MA, for $24.1 million. JLL's Nat Heald and Chris Angelone represented the seller in the transaction. This acquisition marks Urban Edge's first substantial entry into the Boston Metro area, with plans to benefit from the region's growth and potential future redevelopment.

title: TiVo inks $3B merger with Xperi to create new ‘amazing entertainment platform’
summary: TiVo and Xperi are merging in a $3 billion all-stock transaction to create a new "amazing entertainment platform." The deal combines TiVo's content aggregation with Xperi's reach into home, automotive, and mobile tech markets. The new company aims to leverage its combined 10,000 patents to transform the entertainment experience and compete with other content aggregators like Roku and Amazon.

title: Tech innovation is changing the world, and this fund manager has big bets on how it’s going to work
summary: The article profiles Catherine Wood, founder and CEO of ARK Invest, and her strategy of investing in disruptive technologies through exchange-traded funds. Wood, who bought Amazon shares in 2002, believes there are similar opportunities in areas like genomics and autonomous vehicles today, utilizing an "open-source research ecosystem." Her approach contrasts with traditional venture capital by making public market bets rather than private ones.

title: Tech innovation is changing the world, and this fund manager has big bets on how it’s going to work
summary: This article highlights Catherine Wood, founder and CEO of ARK Invest, and her investment strategy focused on disruptive technologies. Wood makes her bets in exchange-traded funds, using an "open-source research ecosystem." Her approach to public markets contrasts with traditional venture capitalists.

title: Rivian Gets $1.3 Billion Investment in Electric Truck Venture (Published 2019)
summary: Rivian, an electric-vehicle start-up backed by Amazon and Ford, announced a $1.3 billion investment led by T. Rowe Price. This funding round, the largest for Rivian to date, brings its total investments for 2019 to $2.85 billion as it prepares to launch its truck and SUV and compete with Tesla. The investment highlights confidence in Rivian's strategy and products, but also its significant capital needs.

title: Joseph Segel: QVC founder has died at 88; he also founded more than 20 other companies, including The Franklin Mint
summary: Joseph Segel, the "quintessential entrepreneur" and founder of the home-shopping network QVC, has died at 88 due to congestive heart failure. Segel, who also founded over 20 other companies including The Franklin Mint, was remembered as a visionary who changed the way the world shops. He retired from QVC in 1993 but remained an adviser until 2013, leaving a legacy of innovation and customer focus.

title: Rivian announces $1.3 billion funding round led by T. Rowe Price
summary: Rivian has closed a $1.3 billion investment round led by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., with participation from Amazon, Ford Motor Company, and BlackRock. This funding marks Rivian's fourth investment announcement of 2019, highlighting strong investor confidence in the electric vehicle manufacturer's team, products, technology, and strategy. The company is preparing to launch its R1T and R1S vehicles, with customer deliveries expected to begin at the end of 2020.

title: Electric-Truck Maker Rivian Raises $1.3 Billion in New Funding
summary: Electric-truck startup Rivian Automotive Inc. has raised an additional $1.3 billion in funding led by T. Rowe Price, bringing its total raised in 2019 to $2.85 billion. This investment, also involving Amazon.com Inc., Ford Motor Co., and BlackRock, aims to support the company's upcoming vehicle rollouts.

title: Joseph Segel, QVC founder, dies at 88
summary: Joseph Segel, the visionary entrepreneur who founded the home-shopping network QVC, has died at 88 due to congestive heart failure. Segel, who also founded the Franklin Mint, was remembered as an innovator whose ideas changed the way the world shops and whose focus on the customer profoundly influenced QVC's culture. He retired as QVC chairman in 1993 but remained an adviser until 2013 and was recognized as one of the greatest business leaders and most influential alumni by Harvard Business School and Wharton School respectively.

title: That U-Haul in your neighborhood may very well be carrying your gift order
summary: During the peak holiday season, delivery companies like UPS resorted to renting U-Haul trucks to manage the surge in package volumes. This strategy allowed them to temporarily expand their fleets and ensure deliveries, supplementing their own drivers and seasonal hires. Amazon also experienced a record-breaking holiday season, with significant increases in Prime Free One-Day and Same-Day delivery services, necessitating a boost in its seasonal workforce.

title: Amazon boxes a holiday gift for paper mills
summary: U.S. paper mills are capitalizing on the "Amazon effect" this holiday season by recycling a surge of used cardboard boxes into new paper products, transitioning from newsprint to containerboard demand driven by e-commerce giants. This shift is crucial following China's 2018 ban on contaminated recyclable imports, which caused a domestic oversupply of cardboard and prompted significant foreign investment in U.S. paper mills. Despite challenges with contamination, the paper industry achieved a record 96% recycling recovery rate for cardboard boxes in 2018, highlighting a successful circular economy model.

title: Kornit Digital CEO: We're aiming for $1b annual sales
summary: Kornit Digital CEO Ronen Samuel outlines an ambitious goal of reaching $1 billion in annual sales, driven by new product launches, geographical expansion, and a focus on sustainable, on-demand digital textile printing. The company aims to capture a 2% share of the 15 billion annual textile printings market by 2023, while also exploring non-organic growth through acquisitions in workflow solutions and machine-related technologies. Samuel emphasizes the company's commitment to growth as an Israeli manufacturing entity, rather than seeking an exit.

title: Lands' End sees positive results in a return to its classic roots
summary: Lands' End is experiencing positive results by returning to its classic roots after previous attempts to become a high-fashion brand failed. Under CEO Jerome Griffith, the company has seen improved sales, a growing customer base, and strategic expansions, including selling on Amazon and opening more standalone stores. Analysts generally express optimism about the brand's "rebirth," though some caution that its future success in 2020 and 2021 remains to be seen.

title: Could Amazon Buy eBay In A 2020 Cash Deal?
summary: This article explores the possibility of Amazon acquiring eBay in a cash deal in 2020, analyzing eBay's struggles, the impact of activist investors, and Amazon's financial capacity. It discusses how eBay's asset-light model offers attractive margins and could complement Amazon's third-party seller services, despite potential antitrust scrutiny. The author also details eBay's history of leadership changes and activist intervention, highlighting the company's declining market share against growing competition.

title: After its strongest year in a decade, Apple stock is historically expensive on a price-to-earnings basis
summary: Apple's stock concluded its strongest year in a decade with its price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio reaching a historic high of 24.7, up from just over 13 at the beginning of 2019. This elevated P/E ratio makes Apple historically expensive compared to its past performance, although it remains below the average for the S&P 500 information technology index and many other megacap tech stocks. Factors like improved iPhone 11 expectations, anticipation of the 5G 2020 iPhone cycle, and strong wearable device performance have contributed to the increased valuation, according to Deutsche Bank analyst Jeriel Ong.
